package fixture

// KNOWN-BAD 1 — the interceptor shape (ServerInterceptors.go:448-452).
// Producer preserved a sentinel; consumer erases it and continues to a verdict.
func badConsumerCollapse(domain, method string) bool {
	infos, err := getActionResourceInfos(domain, method)
	if err != nil {
		logWarn("proceeding with empty resource infos", err)
		infos = make([]*ResourceInfos, 0)
	}
	return validateAction(infos)
}

// KNOWN-BAD 2 — the repository shape (trusted_publisher.go:167-170).
// A failed read is returned as an empty set with a nil error.
func badErrorErased(dir string) ([]*Publisher, error) {
	entries, err := readDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil
	}
	return parse(entries), nil
}

// KNOWN-BAD 3 — the policy shape (signature_policy.go:109-134).
// A decode failure becomes the most permissive posture, then decides.
func badPermissiveDefault(raw []byte) bool {
	policy, err := unmarshalPolicy(raw)
	if err != nil {
		policy = defaultSignaturePolicy()
	}
	return policyDecision(policy)
}

// KNOWN-GOOD 1 — the RBAC timeout shape (ServerInterceptors.go:398-419).
// "a stalled authorization service must NOT silently grant"
func goodDeniesOnError(method string) (bool, error) {
	allowed, err := validateActionRemote(method)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	return allowed, nil
}

// KNOWN-GOOD 2 — logged and carried on, but no verdict downstream.
// Not every swallowed error is an authority collapse.
func goodNoVerdictDownstream(path string) {
	data, err := readFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		logWarn("cache read failed", err)
		data = nil
	}
	writeCache(data)
}

// KNOWN-GOOD 3 — a declared fail-safe, annotated with its reason.
func goodDeclaredFailsafe(method string) bool {
	infos, err := lookup(method)
	//go:uncertainty:declared-failsafe empty set means "unauthenticated allowlist", proven by TestAllowlistBypassesRBAC
	if err != nil {
		infos = nil
	}
	return validateAction(infos)
}

// KNOWN-BAD 4 — an opt-out with no stated reason is itself reported.
func badUnjustifiedOptOut(method string) bool {
	infos, err := lookup(method)
	//go:uncertainty:declared-failsafe
	if err != nil {
		infos = nil
	}
	return validateAction(infos)
}

// KNOWN-GOOD 4 — the cluster-doctor shape. No local guard at all, because
// correctness is centralised in snapshotSourceUnavailableFindings + the ratchet
// test. There is no ERASURE here, so the scanner must stay silent: absence of a
// local guard is explicitly NOT the thing being detected.
func goodCentralisedElsewhere(snap *Snapshot) []Finding {
	if snap.Nodes == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return evaluateRules(snap)
}

// KNOWN-GOOD 5 — node_agent/heartbeat.go:1715. Marking inventory INCOMPLETE on
// error is the honest answer, not an erasure. Fail-closed.
func goodMarksIncompleteOnError(ctx Ctx) Status {
	inventoryComplete := true
	installed, err := computeInstalled(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		logWarn("compute installed services", err)
		inventoryComplete = false
	}
	return resolveStatus(installed, inventoryComplete)
}

// KNOWN-GOOD 6 — mcp/governor.go:417. Recording that a command failed.
func goodRecordsFailure(cmd Cmd) Result {
	var result Result
	err := cmd.Run()
	if err != nil {
		result.Success = false
	}
	return decideBranch(result)
}
